title: Bernardine of Siena (20 May)
hookLine: a preacher who spread the letters IHS as a sign of the Holy Name

lines: A PREACHER HOLDS UP A BOARD.
cards: Three letters. I, H, S. You may have seen them stamped on a communion wafer, stitched on a vestment, carved over a church door, cut into an old gravestone, often with rays of light around them, like a sun.

It's easy to walk past them without asking what they say. In the Italian towns, tradition says, a Franciscan preacher used to hold them up in front of the crowd on a painted board, gold on blue, and ask everyone to look.
Today, the man with the board: Bernardine of Siena.

teach.h: THE LETTERS ARE THE NAME, SHORTENED.
teach.b: First, the letters. IHS is the name Jesus, shortened, from the way it was written in Greek capitals: the first three letters of the name.
Later, people read other meanings into it, Latin phrases that happen to fit the letters. Those are pious readings added afterward; the root is simply the name.

teach.h: A FRIAR PREACHING IN THE SQUARES.
teach.b: Bernardine was a Franciscan friar and a preacher who traveled from town to town.
Tradition says crowds came to hear him in the city squares, and that he preached against feuds and gambling and the hatreds that split towns into factions.

Then he'd lift up the board and invite people to honor the name of Jesus. Some townspeople, tradition says, burned their gaming boards and painted the letters over their own doors. Not everyone loved this.
Some critics accused him of something close to idolatry, as if he were asking people to worship a painted sign.
Tradition says he was examined and cleared. His answer, in effect, was that the board wasn't the point. The name was.
Paul's letter puts it this way, in the Douay-Rheims: "That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth."
For Bernardine, the name was a short way to pray: one word, said with love.

teach.h: IN THE NAME OF JESUS EVERY KNEE SHOULD BOW.
teach.b: Catholics later kept a feast of the Holy Name of Jesus, and the letters he carried spread far beyond the towns where he preached.

how: Catholics remember Saint Bernardine of Siena on 20 May; the IHS monogram he promoted appears on hosts, vestments and church buildings, and the Church keeps a memorial of the Most Holy Name of Jesus on 3 January.

games.why: tradition says he was examined and cleared, and kept preaching the holy name.

practice: If you have paper, a fogged mirror or a note on your phone, write the three letters, I, H, S, and look at them.

If you pray, say the name they stand for slowly, once with each breath, and nothing else; if you don't, simply let the letters be what they are, a name, shortened, that people have carved into wood and stone.

wordCard.voice: IHS, the three letters of the name Jesus that Bernardine of Siena, a Franciscan preacher, held up so crowds would honor the holy name.

carryVoice: Your line: the holy name. Under every later reading, the root is simply a name. Until tomorrow.
